clue.text: Deficit is colossal without fuel

indicators.note: without tells us to take the letters of the fuel out of the longer word

parts.note: coal is a fuel burnt in fires and furnaces

explanation.surface: A huge financial shortfall caused by running out of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, O, A and L, in that order, from COLOSSAL and LOSS is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a shortfall in money, the same thing as a deficit.

clue.text: Mark or Cliff?

definitions.meaning: a blemish left on skin after a wound heals
a steep rocky face on a hillside, a northern English word

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both the lasting trace of an old wound and a craggy rock face on a hill.

clue.text: Char found in stream

definitions.meaning: to scorch or blacken by fire
a small river, the Scottish word

explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to sear with fire, and in Scotland a brook is called by the same word.

clue.text: How important is a six to score?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a tally is a running score or count

explanation.surface: A question about how much a six counts towards a cricket score.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question 'How important?', answered by an adverb that goes before 'important'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb says to what degree something matters, as in essential, crucially so.

clue.text: Doubts of girl about making a donation

indicators.note: about means the word for girl goes around the other piece

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
giving means making a donation

explanation.surface: A young woman has reservations about donating to a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Misgivings are feelings of doubt or apprehension about something.

clue.text: Convincing but unorthodox vice-consul

indicators.note: unorthodox suggests the letters of the diplomat's title are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A deputy consul who is persuasive despite his unconventional ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclusive argument settles the matter, so it is convincing beyond doubt.

clue.text: See first at Bath having girth adjusted? It's a plant!

parts.note: to eye something is to look at or see it

indicators.note: first at tells us to take only the opening letter of the city's name
adjusted signals the letters of girth are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor to Bath has their saddle strap altered, then discovers a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges GIRTH into RIGHT; BATH is the English spa city, giving its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat sore eyes, a genuine herb.

clue.text: To take drugs is a false move

definitions.meaning: to experience a hallucinogenic high, slang

explanation.definitionFit: A hallucinogenic high is slang for drug-taking, and stumbling over something is making a misstep.

clue.text: Snapping from a distance, in short

definitions.text: Snapping from a distance, in short

parts.words: Snapping from a distance, in short
parts.note: a photograph taken of something far away, the word being a shortened form of a longer technical term

explanation.definitionFit: A long-focus lens photographs distant subjects, and its name is clipped from the longer adjective for such photography.

clue.text: But it is not a reduction for psychiatric treatment

definitions.text: But it is not a reduction for psychiatric treatment

parts.words: But it is not a reduction for psychiatric treatment
parts.note: plays on the slang word for a psychiatrist: treatment by such a doctor sounds like a word that actually means getting smaller

explanation.definitionFit: The word means contraction or loss of size, yet read as a psychiatrist's slang name plus a suffix it seems to be therapy.

clue.text: This chap is a Caledonian to the very end

indicators.note: to the very end points to the closing letters of the word, where a man's name sits

explanation.surface: A man is a Scot through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits in the last three letters of 'Caledonian', a poetic word for Scottish, fitting since it is a typical Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Scottish man's first name, so it can stand for some chap.

clue.text: Sections of the competition for members only?

definitions.meaning: stages of a contest, such as rounds of a tournament

explanation.walkthrough: 'members' here means limbs, not club members.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages of a relay or tournament share their name with lower limbs, and limbs are a body's members.

clue.text: Extra over takes energy

parts.note: by can mean over or past, as in time going by
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls one more over, adding some energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batter and keeper untouched, counted as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run conceded without the bat touching the ball is scored as an extra.

clue.text: Telegraphist will give indication to go abroad

parts.note: a sign is an indication
aller is French for to go, i.e. the foreign word

explanation.surface: A telegraph operator will signal for someone to leave the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go abroad' asks for 'to go' in a foreign language: French ALLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraphist sends messages by signals, so is one who transmits signals.

clue.text: Criminal encouraged in the glassworks?

parts.note: a crook who blasts open strongboxes, read as a glassworker who shapes glass by breath and is 'safe' there, i.e. encouraged

explanation.definitionFit: A cracksman uses explosives on strongboxes; in a glassworks a blower would be welcome rather than a criminal.

clue.text: Which chapel, would you say-in the field-uses this chant?

definitions.text: Which chapel, would you say-in the field-uses this chant?

parts.words: Which chapel, would you say-in the field-uses this chant?
parts.note: a question whose spoken reply could be heard as a choice between two men's first names, also naming plainsong sung in church

explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong named after Pope Gregory I is the traditional unaccompanied liturgical singing of the Western church.

clue.text: Results at the farm could be improved

indicators.note: could be improved suggests the letters of the farm phrase are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Harvest returns on the farm leave room for improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftermath means consequences, especially of a disaster, so it stands for results.

clue.text: Make a way for president to receive greeting

parts.note: ave is the Latin word of greeting, hail

explanation.surface: Clearing the path for a head of state who is to be welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave is to lay a surface for a road, literally making a way.

clue.text: Movables of 15?

definitions.meaning: personal property that can be carried, belongings
the answer to 15 down, results or consequences

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the solution to 15 down, results, whose synonym also means consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal belongings are a person's possessions, and consequences are the outcomes of a cause.

clue.text: Silver circle on the beach

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a circle

explanation.surface: A silver ring lying on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranded ship is stuck on the shore, beached.

clue.text: A profit on street or counter?

parts.note: gain means profit

explanation.surface: Asking whether a profit made on a high street or over a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like the shop fitting but is a preposition meaning opposed to.
explanation.definitionFit: To act counter to something is to act in opposition to it.

clue.text: Unusual bore for river in Spain

indicators.note: unusual tells us to take the letters of bore in a strange order

explanation.surface: A tidal wave is a rare sight on a Spanish river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is the longest river flowing wholly within Spain, reaching the Mediterranean.

clue.text: I get hours of variety that is blameless

indicators.note: of variety suggests the letters are given in a varied order

explanation.surface: Someone with a varied work schedule insists they are beyond reproach.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone righteous is morally upright and so without fault.

clue.text: Tree under threat from hotel management

indicators.note: from says the letters come out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tree is endangered by the hotel managers who want to cut it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a tree under threat from Dutch elm disease.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree has been ravaged across Britain by a fungal disease, so it is a threatened species.

clue.text: Farm butter?

parts.note: not the dairy spread but an animal on the farm that butts with its head

explanation.definitionFit: A male sheep charges with its horns, so it is a farmyard creature that butts.

clue.text: Lid put on baked beans!

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat, and beans is slang for heads baked by the sun

explanation.definitionFit: A pith helmet is a sun hat worn in hot countries to protect the head from heat.

clue.text: Evening for taking aside, politically!

definitions.meaning: joining with a party or bloc, taking a side

explanation.walkthrough: 'aside' is read as 'a side': siding with a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing things into line is evening them up, and a nation's political allegiance is its stance with a bloc.

clue.text: Symbol of distinction

definitions.meaning: a written sign for a musical sound

explanation.definitionFit: A musical sign on a stave is one sense, and fame or eminence is another, as in someone of renown.

clue.text: Common grub found in wheat stalks

indicators.note: found in says the letters are located inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A larva living in the stems of a wheat crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, so a homely word for grub.

clue.text: Sound horn, going either way

indicators.note: going either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A driver blasts a horn at traffic coming from both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow a car or ship's hooter is to give a short blast on it.

clue.text: Article in study of university official

indicators.note: in tells us the article goes inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article in a learned study about a university administrator.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean heads a faculty or college, an academic officer.

clue.text: Stumbling that can get us lost

definitions.text: Stumbling that can get us lost

parts.words: Stumbling that can get us lost
parts.note: a falter or pause, recalling the proverb that whoever delays is lost

explanation.definitionFit: Faltering before acting is pausing in doubt, and the proverb warns that delay leads to ruin.
